Aha! After Qxb5+, White has NO captures available. The knight can't take on d6. So Black simply wins the pawn and gets a good position. This is the cleanest win.

**Best move: Qxb5**

**Main line:** 1...Qxb5+ 2.Kg1 (or Ke1), and Black is up a clean pawn with no compensation for White.

**Motif:** hangingPiece (the b5 pawn is undefended and can be captured with check)

---

## Coaching Note (80 words):

When your opponent plays a move, always scan for undefended pieces before calculating complex tactics. After White played Nf5, the pawn on b5 was left hanging. Notice that Qxb5 gives check—this means White must move the king instead of recapturing or creating threats. Always prefer the move that wins material cleanly with the initiative (check or threat) over speculative attacks. This simple principle will win you many games at club level.
